newsitem.title: USA: Washington mayor seeks death for police killers.
newsitem.headline: Washington mayor seeks death for police killers.

text.p: Agonizing over the shooting deaths of two Washington police officers, Mayor Marion Barry on Monday urged that the death penalty be instituted in the U.S. capital for those who kill police.

"For many years, I have opposed capital punishment," Barry said in a statement. "However, in recent weeks, I have agonized over the senseless slaying of police officers Brian T. Gibson and Oliver Wendell Smith, Jr. I am troubled by the fact that these officers apparently were killed because they were police officers."
Gibson and Smith were shot to death in February in separate incidents.
In legislation sent to the District of Columbia city council, Barry proposed giving the death penalty to those who murder police or other law enforcement officers.
The death penalty could not be imposed unless aggravating circumstances -- such as robbery, carjacking, arson or rape -- occurred in the commission of the murder of the officer, the statement said.

Under current law, the penalty for first degree murder in Washington is life in prison without the possibility of parole. There has been no enforceable death penalty statute in the U.S. capital since 1972.
